{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "The taskSchema requires all fields (id, title, completed, createdAt, updatedAt) and disallows additional properties, but PATCH is documented as accepting partial request bodies such as {\"completed\":true}. The spec does not define a separate PATCH request schema, so a client or code generator applying the same taskSchema to PATCH would incorrectly reject valid partial updates.",
    "The error format is only illustrated with one example (TASK_NOT_FOUND), while 400 is listed for four endpoints. There are no defined error codes/messages for invalid UUIDs, missing title, malformed JSON, unknown fields, or attempts to modify read-only fields. This makes client error handling underspecified.",
    "GET /tasks returns a bare array with no pagination, cursor, or limit/offset parameters. The proposal acknowledges this as a future breaking change, but for a collection that can grow, the response is unbounded and clients cannot incrementally fetch results without a later API version.",
    "The spec does not define how the server assigns id, createdAt, and updatedAt for POST or how updatedAt changes on PATCH. While the schema marks them readOnly, the endpoint descriptions do not state the exact server responsibility, leaving implementers to guess."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Add separate schema definitions for create and update requests, e.g., TaskCreate with required title and optional description/completed, and TaskUpdate with all optional fields and additionalProperties:false. Explicitly state that id, createdAt, and updatedAt are server-managed and must not be accepted in requests.",
    "Expand the errorFormat section with concrete 400 examples and code values, such as VALIDATION_ERROR, INVALID_UUID, and READ_ONLY_FIELD, and list the error codes associated with each endpoint.",
    "Consider returning a paginated envelope immediately (e.g., {\"items\":[...], \"nextCursor\":...}) or at least specifying query parameters such as limit/offset/cursor. If pagination remains a non-goal, document the maximum response size or deprecation strategy.",
    "Add a short section specifying that authentication is out of scope or explicitly requiring an Authorization header when the API is deployed in a multi-tenant or public setting."
  ]
}
